correctness.rationale: Every edge generator is a squarefree two-vertex support; a nonleaf--nonleaf edge forces a full-support collision and all other graphs have private variables per edge. A P4 contributes exactly seven LCM supports, and edge additions cannot increase normalized cardinality. In the critical window, triangles and four-edge connected subgraphs vanish, and factorial moments give a Poisson(c^3/2) count of P4 components. At higher densities, coupling, second moments and a conflict-graph independence bound give arbitrarily many disjoint P4s and hence density tending to zero. verify.py exhaustively tested every simple graph through six vertices, density monotonicity through five vertices and independent path product examples; the general proof is analytic and does not rely on finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The graph edge-ideal normalized LCM-lattice size is the natural invariant explicitly posed in recent commutative algebra literature. Rather than an arbitrary finite computation, this theorem finds the exact threshold, the entire nondegenerate critical probability law, the limiting expectation and a deterministic maximum-lattice characterization. It locates a distinct algebraic transition before the giant component in every growing-vertex finite-field-independent degree-two model. The elementary finite criterion alone is not the claimed value; the motivated random model and universal limiting theorem are.
